title: Why Does a Spinning Coin Speed Up Before It Stops?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why does a spinning coin speed up before it stops?
The rattle gets faster and faster, then suddenly, silence.
But late in the spin, the coin's face is barely turning.
What speeds up is the point where the edge touches the table.
As the coin loses energy, it leans lower.
And the lower it leans, the faster that touching point races around the circle.
Each lap adds a tap on the table, so the rattle rises.
Near the end, it laps tens of times a second, then the coin drops flat.
The coin is losing energy. Only the touching point speeds up.
